VII.}}</noinclude>said to him, ''Loose of the shoe of thy feete: for the place vvherein thou standest, is {{sup|‖}} holy ground''. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=34}}† ''Seeing I haue seen the affliction of my people vvhich is in Ægypt, and I haue heard their groning, and am descended to deliuer them. And novv come, and I vvil send thee into Ægypt''. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=35}}† This Moyses, vvhom they denied, saying, ''Vvho hath appointed the prince and Captaine''? him God sent prince & {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Christ is our Redeemer, and yet Moyses is here called redeemer. so Christ is our Mediator and Aduocate, and yet we may haue Saincts our inferior mediators and aduocates also. ''See Annot. 1 Io. 2, 1''.}}∷ redeemer, vvith the hand of the Angel that appeared to him in the bush. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=36}}† He {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 7. 8. 9. 10. 11. 12, 37.''}}* brought them forth doing vvonders and signes in the land of Ægypt, and in the redde sea, and in the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 16.''}}* desert fourtie yeres. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=37}}† This is that Moyses vvhich said to the children of Israël, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 18.''}}* ''A prophet vvil God raise vp to you of your ovvne brethren as my self: him you shal heare''. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=38}}† This is he that {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 19, 3. 19.''}}* vvas in the assemblie in the vvildernesse, vvith the Angel that spake to him in Mount-Sina, and vvith our fathers: vvho receiued the vvordes of life to giue vnto vs. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=39}}† To vvhom our fathers vvould not be obedient: but they repelled him, and in their hartes turned avvay into Aegypt, {{verse|chapter=7|verse=40}}† saying to Aaron: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 32, 1.''}}* ''Make vs goddes that may goe before vs. for this Moyses that brought vs out of the land of Aegypt, vve knovv not vvhat is befallen to him''. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=41}}† And they made a calfe in those daies, and offered sacrifice to the Idol, and reioyced in the vvorkes of their ovvne handes. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=42}}† And God turned, and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Amos. 5, 25.''}}* deliuered them vp {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''λατρεύειν.''}}∷ to serue the host of heauen, as it is vvritten in the booke of the Prophets: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ For a iust punishment of their former offenses God gaue them vp to vvorke vvhat vvickednes they vvould them selues, as it is said of the Gentils ''Rom. 1''.}}∷ ''Did you offer victims and hostes vnto me fourtie yeres in the desert, O house of Israël''? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=43}}† ''And you tooke vnto you the tabernacle of Moloch, and the starre of your God Rempham, figures vvhich you made, to adore them. And I vvil translate you beyond Babylon''.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=44}}† The tabernacle of testimonie vvas among our fathers in the desert, as God ordained speaking to Moyses, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 25, 40.''}}* ''that he should make it according to the forme vvhich he had seen''. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=45}}† Vvhich our fathers {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ios. 3, 14.''}}* vvith {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ This is Iosuè, so called in Greeke in type of our Sauiour.}}∷ Iesus receiuing, brought it in also into the possession of the Gentiles, vvhich God expelled from the face of our fathers, till in the daies of Dauid, {{verse|chapter=7|verse=46}}† Vvho found grace before God, and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 131, 5.''}}* desired that he might finde a tabernacle for the God of Iacob. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=47}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''1. Par. 17.''}}* Salomon built him a house. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=48}}† But the Highest dvvelleth {{sup|‖}} not in houses {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 17. 25.''}}* made by hand, as the prophet saith: {{verse|chapter=7|verse=49}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 66, 1.''}}* ''Heauen is my seate: and the earth the foote-stole of my feete. Vvhat house vvil you build me, saith our Lord? or vvhat place is there of my resting''? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=50}}† ''Hath not my hand made al these things''?

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=51}}† You stiffe-necked and of vncircumcised hartes and eares, you alvvaies resist the holy Ghost: as your fathers, your selues also. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=52}}† Vvhich of the prophets did not your fathers<noinclude>{{rh|||persecute?}}</noinclude>
